# Answer: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is:

> **Sort the nonzero row-0 command codes numerically, then apply them, instead of preserving their left-to-right order.**

This shortcut fits **all three labeled canonical pairs**, not merely the two visible training demonstrations. The canonical `[3,1]` example looks order-sensitive at the command level, but its particular body has an accidental symmetry that makes `[3,1]` and sorted `[1,3]` produce the same label.

An exact counterexample emitted by the repaired generator is seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `easy`:

```text
3 0 0 0 0 0 1
0 5 5 0 0 0 0
0 5 5 5 0 0 0
0 0 5 0 0 0 0
0 0 5 0 0 0 0
```

The intended commands are `[3,1]`: rotate clockwise, then flip left/right. The selected Racket authority returns:

```text
5 5 0 0
5 5 5 5
0 5 0 0
```

The sorted-command rival executes `[1,3]` and returns:

```text
0 0 5 0
5 5 5 5
0 0 5 5
```

I checked the intended output with the supported source-bound command:

```text
python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 01ab62800c73 \
  --input ../checks/counterexample/input.json \
  --out ../checks/counterexample/racket.json
```

The receipt binds generator SHA-256 `449c1d95c75158329e3b497aa724f1124f613e6442433a626c13a4cf72527318` and rule hash `6f47f78828c8`; it matches the independent Python rule mirror and disagrees with the rival. Exact grids and hashes are retained in `repo/generators/01ab62800c73/counterexamples/sort-commands-fits-canonical.json` and `checks/counterexample/`.

Yes—the proposed generator deliberately emits such cases. Default multi-command sequences are filtered so their intended result differs from sorted, first-only, and last-only execution. The four-profile lesson schedule includes these witnesses, and both the exhaustive fixed-seed schedule receipt and the 300-lesson census refute `sort_commands` in every materialized lesson and every tested query rotation.
